finding.title: Replace wall-clock Future.delayed synchronization with deterministic waits in gamification staleness tests
finding.why: 7 sites across 2 files (curriculum_breakdown_staleness_test.dart:66; points_providers_reactive_test.dart:61,68,100,111,154,164) synchronize on a Riverpod stream/FutureProvider re-emission by sleeping a fixed real-world duration instead of awaiting the actual event — the same feature area's achievements_overview_staleness_after_redemption_test.dart shows the deterministic alternative already in use (container.invalidate(...) + await container.read(provider.future)). A fixed delay is a flaky-under-CI-load bet: too short and a legitimately-fixed provider that happens to take longer intermittently fails the test; the tests exist specifically to pin reactive-update timing, so racing against the clock to verify timing is a contradiction in terms.
finding.recommendation: Await the stream's next matching emission via a Completer or StreamQueue keyed on the expected value (or pumpEventQueue() for Drift's microtask-driven watch streams) instead of a fixed delay.
acceptance_criteria: Zero `Future<void>.delayed` calls remain in curriculum_breakdown_staleness_test.dart and points_providers_reactive_test.dart.
Both files pass 20 consecutive runs under --test-randomize-ordering-seed=random without flake.

finding.title: Rename StreakStateProvider — it is a plain service class, not a @riverpod provider

evidence.quote:
class StreakStateProvider {
  StreakStateProvider({required UserDatabase db, required LocalDayClock clock})

finding.why: The file/class name (streak_state_provider.dart, StreakStateProvider) matches the app-wide convention for @riverpod codegen providers, but this is a hand-written plain class with no @riverpod annotation, no part '*.g.dart', and no Notifier/AsyncNotifier base — it's constructed directly by 5 different callers (parent_dashboard_aggregator.dart, streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart, streak_alert_service.dart, streak_service.dart, dashboard_providers.dart). An auditor or agent grepping for '_provider.dart' files to apply the SM-1..8 rule family would misclassify this file and either skip real SM-7 questions (is it constructed only inside a real provider?) or misapply provider-specific rules that don't fit a plain service.
finding.recommendation: Rename to streak_state_service.dart / StreakStateService (or similar) to match its actual role.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'class StreakStateProvider' lib/ returns zero hits after rename; all 5 call sites updated.

finding.title: StreakEvent domain class name collides with the Drift-generated StreakEvent row class

evidence.quote:
/// Distinct from Drift's row class (also called `StreakEvent` and
/// generated from `tables/streak_events.dart`): this one is what the

finding.why: lib/features/gamification/streak/streak_event.dart and the Drift-generated lib/core/database/user/user_database.g.dart both define a top-level class named StreakEvent. The doc comment shows the author was aware and every consumer (streak_event_log.dart, streak_restorer.dart, streak_state_provider.dart) works around it with `import '...user_database.dart' hide StreakEvent`, so today it's contained — but per AG-4's own rationale, agents/devs locate code by grep, and 'class StreakEvent' now returns two unrelated definitions; a new file that imports user_database.dart without remembering the hide clause gets an ambiguous-import compile error rather than a clean import.
finding.recommendation: Rename the domain value type (e.g. StreakLogEvent or StreakDomainEvent) so the name is unique across lib/.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn '^class StreakEvent\b' lib/ (excluding .g.dart) returns exactly one hit under the new name; the `hide StreakEvent` import qualifiers become unnecessary and are removed.
